steps.title: Words → maths
steps.intro: Translate one phrase at a time — then answer what they actually asked.

head: Words
Maths
rows: The difference between A and B is 12
3 notebooks cost the same as 5 pens
The ratio of A to B is \(2:3\)

tips: Three stages: translate → solve → answer what they asked.
Long question? Work step by step — one phrase at a time.

steps.stem: Six trays hold 42 biscuits. At the same number per tray, how many biscuits fit on 15 trays?
explanation: Across in the ratio table: \(\frac{42}{6}=7\) biscuits per tray.
15 trays: \(15\cdot7=105\) biscuits.

steps.stem: At a constant pace, a student completes 12 exercises in 8 minutes. How many exercises does she complete in 14 minutes?
explanation: Across and down are not whole numbers. Triangle value: \(\frac{14\cdot12}{8}=\frac{14\cdot3}{2}=21\).
Sense check: 14 minutes is less than twice 8 minutes. The answer must be less than \(2\cdot12=24\) ✓.

steps.stem: Six workers paint a hall in 10 days. All the workers work at the same rate. How many days would 4 workers need to paint the same hall?
explanation: Fewer workers need more days. The answer must be more than 10.
The work stays the same: \(6\cdot10=60\) worker-days.
\(4\cdot d=60\), therefore \(d=\frac{60}{4}=15\) days.
The trap: the ratio table gives \(\frac{4\cdot10}{6}=6\frac23\) — fewer days with fewer workers, which is impossible.

steps.stem: A bakery sells a tart for 58 credits. Making it uses 300 g of pastry at 6 credits per 100 g, 200 g of filling at 9 credits per 100 g, and 4 berries at half a credit each. Ignoring other costs, what is the selling price minus ingredient cost?
explanation: Pastry: \(3\cdot6=18\). Filling: \(2\cdot9=18\). Berries: \(4\cdot\frac12=2\).
Ingredient cost: \(18+18+2=38\) credits.
Selling price minus cost: \(58-38=20\) credits. (38 is the cost — not what they asked.)

steps.stem: Hire company A charges 3 credits for every minute or part of a minute. Company B charges 14 credits for every 5-minute block or part of a block. What is the difference between the charges for an 11.5-minute hire?
explanation: Company A: 11.5 minutes are paid as 12 minutes ("or part of a minute"): \(12\cdot3=36\) credits.
Company B: two blocks cover only 10 minutes. 11.5 minutes need 3 blocks: \(3\cdot14=42\) credits.
Difference: \(42-36=6\) credits.

steps.title: Ratios and equal ratios
steps.intro: The ratio table and the ratio facts you will use all through the course.

tables.title: Equal ratios (ratio table)
head: Situation
Method
rows: Across or down is a whole number
triangle value: diagonal product ÷ the remaining number
cross-multiply: the diagonal products are equal
One goes up, the other goes down (workers and days)
inverse: the product stays the same, \(6\cdot10=4\cdot15\)

tables.title: Ratio facts
head: Fact
Example
rows: No amounts from a ratio alone

tips: Read in order: the first name goes with the first number. The exam tests this.
Before you calculate: should the answer be bigger or smaller?
Counting people? The total must be divisible by the sum of the ratio numbers.

steps.stem: In a class, boys make up \(\frac38\) of all students. Which could be the difference between the numbers of girls and boys?
explanation: Boys \(=3x\) and all \(=8x\). Girls \(=8x-3x=5x\).
Difference: \(5x-3x=2x\). It must be even.
Only 18 is even. Check: \(x=9\) gives 27 boys and 45 girls, and \(45-27=18\) ✓.

steps.stem: The prices of a scooter and a small car are in the ratio \(3:8\). The car costs 15,000 credits more. What is their combined price?
explanation: Scooter \(=3x\), car \(=8x\). Difference: \(8x-3x=5x=15{,}000\), therefore \(x=3{,}000\).
Combined: \(3x+8x=11x=33{,}000\) credits.

steps.stem: In a choir, the ratio of sopranos to altos is \(2:3\), and the ratio of altos to tenors is \(4:5\). There are 30 tenors. How many singers are in the choir?
explanation: Make the altos the same number in both ratios: \(2:3=8:12\) and \(4:5=12:15\).
The ratio of sopranos to altos to tenors is \(8:12:15\).
Tenors: \(15x=30\), therefore \(x=2\).
The trap: the ratio \(2:3:5\) is wrong, because the 3 and the 4 are not the same altos. It gives 60.

steps.stem: In a club, the ratio of boys to girls is \(5:4\). Then 10 boys leave the club, and the ratio of boys to girls becomes \(5:6\). How many members did the club have at first?
explanation: The girls do not change. Make them the same number in both ratios: \(5:4=15:12\) and \(5:6=10:12\).
The boys went down by \(15-10=5\) units. These are the 10 boys who left, therefore 1 unit \(=2\).
At first: \(15+12=27\) units \(=27\cdot2=54\) members.
With an equation: boys \(5x\), girls \(4x\). \(\frac{5x-10}{4x}=\frac56\) gives \(30x-60=20x\), therefore \(x=6\) and \(9x=54\).

steps.stem: A center plans to put the same number of students in each of 6 rooms. One room becomes a storeroom. Each of the 5 remaining rooms must then hold 3 more students. How many students per room were originally planned?
explanation: Planned students per room \(=x\). The number of students does not change: \(6x=5(x+3)\).
They asked for the planned number: 15. (18 is the new number per room.)

steps.title: Give It to the Little Guy

steps.stem: Iris is 6 years older than Leo. Four years ago, Iris was twice Leo’s age. How old is Leo now?
explanation: Leo now \(=x\), Iris now \(=x+6\). Write a row for each time:
\(\begin{array}{l|c|c} & \text{Leo} & \text{Iris} \\ \hline \text{now} & x & x+6 \\ \text{4 years ago} & x-4 & x+2 \end{array}\)
Four years ago Iris was twice Leo. The \(\times2\) goes on the smaller side: \(2(x-4)=x+2\).
\(2x-8=x+2\), therefore \(x=10\). Check: four years ago they were 6 and 12 ✓.

steps.stem: A shopper has 84 credits, enough for 5 identical notebooks but not enough for 6. Which could be the price of one notebook?
explanation: Price \(=p\). Enough for 5: \(5p\le84\), therefore \(p\le16.8\).
Not enough for 6: \(6p>84\), therefore \(p>14\).

steps.stem: One credit buys 2 oranges, 3.5 pears, or 8 plums, with costs proportional to quantity. What is the cost of 6 oranges, 5 pears, and 8 plums? Fractional credits may be paid.
explanation: Oranges: 1 credit buys 2, therefore 6 oranges cost 3 credits. Plums: 8 plums cost 1 credit.
Pears: \(\frac{5\cdot1}{3.5}=\frac{10}{7}\) credits (multiply top and bottom by 2, not by 10).
Total: \(3+1+\frac{10}{7}=\frac{38}{7}\) credits.

steps.stem: A selection program starts with 144 applicants. At the end of each round, \(\frac56\) of the applicants who began that round remain. How many remain after two rounds?
explanation: Round 1: \(144\cdot\frac56=120\). Round 2 acts on 120: \(120\cdot\frac56=100\).
Or write it all first: \(144\cdot\frac56\cdot\frac56=144\cdot\frac{25}{36}=4\cdot25=100\).

steps.stem: There are \(\frac35\) as many apprentices as supervisors in a room. What fraction of all the people are apprentices?
explanation: The ratio of apprentices to supervisors is \(3:5\).
Plug in: 5 supervisors and 3 apprentices, 8 people in all.
Apprentices are \(\frac38\) of all the people. (\(\frac35\) compares them with the supervisors only.)

steps.stem: A grower sends 4 times as many pears to shops as to a market. One quarter of the shop pears and one third of the market pears are rejected. What fraction of all the pears is rejected?
explanation: Only a fraction is asked. Plug in: 3 market pears and \(4\cdot3=12\) shop pears.
Rejected: \(\frac14\cdot12=3\) and \(\frac13\cdot3=1\). In all, 4 out of 15.
The fraction rejected is \(\frac4{15}\). Check: it is between \(\frac14\) and \(\frac13\) ✓.

steps.stem: A maker owns red and blue tiles. She gives away \(\frac14\) of the red tiles and \(\frac16\) of the blue tiles, always giving whole tiles. The remaining color counts are 9 and 20, in an unknown order. How many tiles did she own originally?
explanation: Red left \(=\frac34\) of the red tiles, a whole number of quarters times 3. It must be divisible by 3: 9 can be red, 20 cannot.
Red: \(\frac34R=9\), therefore \(R=12\). Blue: \(\frac56B=20\), therefore \(B=24\).
At first: \(12+24=36\) tiles.

steps.stem: Club A has 3 times as many members as Club B. Three members move from A to B. Afterwards B has half as many members as A. How many members do the clubs have altogether?
explanation: B \(=x\), A \(=3x\). After the move: B has \(x+3\), A has \(3x-3\).
B is half of A: \(2(x+3)=3x-3\), therefore \(2x+6=3x-3\) and \(x=9\).
Total: \(x+3x=4x=36\). (The move does not change the total.)

steps.stem: A freelancer receives a fixed monthly payment plus the same extra amount for each completed task. Ten tasks bring 320 credits; six tasks bring 208 credits. What is the payment per task?
explanation: What changed? \(10-6=4\) more tasks and \(320-208=112\) more credits.
Per task: \(\frac{112}{4}=28\) credits. The fixed payment is the same in both months, and it cancels.

steps.stem: Eight large blocks and twelve small blocks weigh 1,000 g altogether. All large blocks have equal weight, and all small blocks have equal weight. How much do ten large and fifteen small blocks weigh?
explanation: \(8\to10\) and \(12\to15\): both counts are multiplied by \(\frac54\).
Every part grows by the same factor. The weight grows the same way: \(1{,}000\cdot\frac54=1{,}250\) g.
We cannot find one block alone (one equation, two unknowns), but we do not need to.

steps.stem: Ari and Bea have 60 counters altogether. Ari gives Bea 9 counters, after which they have equal numbers. What was Ari’s original count divided by Bea’s original count?
explanation: The total stays 60. Equal at the end: 30 and 30.
Go back: Ari had \(30+9=39\) and Bea had \(30-9=21\).

steps.stem: A pen costs \(x\) credits. A notebook costs 3 credits more than a pen. How much do \(y\) pens and \(y\) notebooks cost altogether?
explanation: Choose numbers: \(x=2\), \(y=3\). A pen costs 2 and a notebook costs 5.
Three pens and three notebooks: \(3\cdot2+3\cdot5=6+15=21\).
Or build it: one pen and one notebook cost \(x+(x+3)=2x+3\). Then \(y\) of each cost \(y(2x+3)\).

steps.stem: A parking lot has 30 vehicles: cars and motorcycles. Each car has 4 wheels, and each motorcycle has 2 wheels. There are 96 wheels in total. How many motorcycles are in the parking lot?
explanation: Assume all 30 are motorcycles: \(30\cdot2=60\) wheels.
Missing: \(96-60=36\) wheels. Each car adds \(4-2=2\) wheels, therefore there are \(\frac{36}{2}=18\) cars.
Faster: assume all are cars (\(120\) wheels). \(120-96=24\) too many, and each motorcycle removes 2: \(\frac{24}{2}=12\) motorcycles.

steps.title: General problems — toolkit
steps.intro: No formula for these — pick the tool that fits the question.

head: Tool
When
Example
rows: a rate like "1 credit buys 3.5 pears"
the ratio \(A:S=3:5\), A out of all \(=\frac38\)
the total lies between the two rates
ratios \(3:1\) and \(2:1\) → total is divisible by 4 and by 3
\(x=2,\ y=3\) → keep the choices that give the same result
all motorcycles: \(30\cdot2=60\) wheels; each car adds 2
only a multiple of the equation can be found

tips: Plug in the answers? Start with the case that has fewer items — easier to calculate.
Found x? Check it is what they asked before you circle.
One thing is twice another? The \(\times2\) goes on the smaller side: \(B=x\), \(A=2x\).
Choose numbers: not 0, not 1, and different for each letter.

steps.stem: A delivery drone can travel 540 km while carrying 80 g. Each extra gram reduces its range by 4 km. What is its range when carrying 113 g?
explanation: Extra load: \(113-80=33\) g.
Lost range: \(33\cdot4=132\) km.

steps.stem: Three teams have 3, 4, and 5 members. They split a 660-credit equipment bill in proportion to team size. How much does the three-person team pay?
explanation: Total people: \(3+4+5=12\).
Per person: \(\frac{660}{12}=55\) credits.
The three-person team pays \(3\cdot55=165\) credits.

steps.stem: A grower has \(x\) trays. Each tray contains \(x\) pots, and each pot contains 2 seedlings. How many seedlings are there?
explanation: Pots: \(x\cdot x=x^2\). Seedlings: \(2\cdot x^2=2x^2\).
Check with \(x=3\): 3 trays of 3 pots is 9 pots and 18 seedlings. \(2\cdot3^2=18\) ✓.

steps.stem: One crest equals 8 sparks. One crest is worth \(\frac25\) of a crown. How many sparks are worth one crown?
explanation: One crest \(=8\) sparks \(=\frac25\) crown.
\(\frac15\) crown \(=\frac82=4\) sparks. One crown \(=5\cdot4=20\) sparks.

steps.stem: A water tank is \(\frac35\) full. After 28 liters are added, it is \(\frac45\) full. What is its capacity?
explanation: \(\frac45-\frac35=\frac15\) of the tank is 28 liters.
Capacity: \(5\cdot28=140\) liters.

steps.stem: A craft stall charges 8 credits to enter a workshop plus 3 credits per item made. Another stall charges no entry fee and 5 credits per item. For how many items are the costs equal?
explanation: Number of items \(=n\): \(8+3n=5n\), therefore \(2n=8\) and \(n=4\).
Check: \(8+3\cdot4=20=5\cdot4\) ✓.

steps.stem: Lena donates \(\frac14\) of her earnings, then spends 180 credits. She has 720 credits left. What were her earnings?
explanation: Before spending 180 credits she had \(720+180=900\).
That is the \(\frac34\) left after the donation: \(\frac34E=900\), therefore \(E=900\cdot\frac43=1{,}200\).

steps.stem: A jar contains 120 spoonfuls of cocoa and costs 18 credits. A bag contains 300 spoonfuls of sugar and costs 12 credits. What is the ingredient cost of a drink using two spoonfuls of cocoa and three of sugar?
explanation: Cocoa: \(\frac{18}{120}=0.15\) credits a spoonful. Sugar: \(\frac{12}{300}=0.04\) credits a spoonful.

steps.stem: A museum sells 4 adult tickets for the same total price as 7 child tickets. Two adults and seven children pay 84 credits. What does an adult ticket cost?
explanation: 7 child tickets cost the same as 4 adult tickets.
Two adults and seven children cost the same as \(2+4=6\) adult tickets: \(6A=84\).
\(A=\frac{84}{6}=14\) credits.

steps.stem: 130 students and 9 teachers go on a trip. A bus carries at most 45 people and costs 800 credits to rent. What is the lowest possible cost of the buses?
explanation: \(3\cdot45=135<139\). Three buses are not enough, therefore they need 4 buses.
Cost: \(4\cdot800=3{,}200\) credits.

steps.stem: The ratio of \(A\) to \(B\) is \(3:4\), and the ratio of \(B\) to \(C\) is \(6:5\). What is the ratio of \(A\) to \(C\)?
explanation: Make \(B\) the same number in both ratios: \(3:4=9:12\) and \(6:5=12:10\).
The ratio \(A:B:C=9:12:10\), therefore \(A:C=9:10\).
The trap: the ratio \(3:5\) puts two different \(B\) numbers together.

steps.stem: A food supply lasts 30 hikers for 12 days. Six more hikers join at the start, and everyone eats the same amount each day. How many days will the supply last?
explanation: More hikers, fewer days. The answer is less than 12.
The supply: \(30\cdot12=360\) hiker-days.
\(36\cdot d=360\), therefore \(d=10\) days.

steps.stem: A reference book costs 18 credits more than a notebook. Four reference books cost the same as six notebooks. What does one reference book cost?
explanation: Notebook \(=n\), reference book \(=n+18\).
Four reference books cost the same as six notebooks: \(4(n+18)=6n\).
\(4n+72=6n\), therefore \(2n=72\) and \(n=36\). Reference book: \(36+18=54\) credits.

steps.stem: A collection has blue, green, and orange tiles. There are 3 times as many blue tiles as green tiles, and twice as many green tiles as orange tiles. Which total is possible?
explanation: Orange \(=x\), green \(=2x\), blue \(=3\cdot2x=6x\).
Total: \(x+2x+6x=9x\). The total must be divisible by 9.
Only \(27=9\cdot3\) works.

steps.stem: Five sketchpads cost as much as two folders and six pencils. A folder costs 3 times as much as a pencil. How many folders cost as much as ten sketchpads?
explanation: Pencil \(=1\) unit, folder \(=3\) units.
Five sketchpads \(=2\cdot3+6\cdot1=12\) units. Ten sketchpads \(=24\) units.
Folders: \(\frac{24}{3}=8\).

steps.stem: A festival has \(\frac56\) as many visitors as local residents. Visitors make up what fraction of all the people at the festival?
explanation: Plug in: 6 residents and \(\frac56\cdot6=5\) visitors.
All the people: \(6+5=11\).
Visitors out of all the people: \(\frac5{11}\). (The denominator must include both groups.)

steps.stem: An older dog is 6 years older than a younger dog. The ratio of their ages now is \(4:1\). What will the ratio of the older dog’s age to the younger dog’s age be in 2 years?
explanation: Older \(=4u\), younger \(=u\). The gap: \(4u-u=3u=6\), therefore \(u=2\).
Now: 8 and 2. In 2 years: 10 and 4.
The ratio is \(10:4=5:2\).

steps.stem: A school orders blue and white folders in the ratio \(5:7\). After 18 blue folders are added, the two colors have equal counts. How many folders were in the original order?
explanation: Blue \(=5x\), white \(=7x\). After adding 18 blue: \(5x+18=7x\), therefore \(2x=18\) and \(x=9\).
Original order: \(12x=12\cdot9=108\).

steps.stem: In a club, the ratio of boys to girls is \(4:3\). Then 6 more girls join, and the numbers of boys and girls become equal. How many members does the club have now?
explanation: The boys do not change. The ratio is \(4:3\) before and \(4:4\) after.
The girls went up by 1 unit. That is the 6 new girls, therefore 1 unit \(=6\).
Now: \(4+4=8\) units \(=48\) members (24 boys and 24 girls).

steps.stem: Iris and Owen have 30 counters altogether. Iris gives Owen 9 counters and then has 4 fewer than Owen. What was the ratio of Iris’s counters to Owen’s before the transfer?
explanation: After the transfer the total is still 30, and Owen has 4 more than Iris.
Iris \(=x\), Owen \(=x+4\): \(x+(x+4)=30\), therefore \(2x=26\) and \(x=13\). Iris has 13 and Owen has 17.
Go back: Iris had \(13+9=22\) and Owen had \(17-9=8\).
The ratio is \(22:8=11:4\).

steps.stem: For 6 days, a camper gathers 25 berries a day and eats \(x\) of them each day. The saved berries then last 18 days at 5 berries a day. What is \(x\)?
explanation: Saved berries: \(18\cdot5=90\).
Gathered: \(6\cdot25=150\). Eaten in 6 days: \(150-90=60\).

steps.stem: A manual contains 48,000 words and 40 diagrams. A leaflet contains 3,000 words and 15 diagrams. The word-to-diagram ratio of the manual is how many times that of the leaflet?
explanation: Manual: \(\frac{48{,}000}{40}=1{,}200\) words per diagram. Leaflet: \(\frac{3{,}000}{15}=200\) words per diagram.

steps.stem: A workshop has 42 stools and carts altogether. Each stool has 3 legs and each cart has 4 wheels. The total number of legs and wheels is 146. How many carts are there?
explanation: Assume all 42 items are stools: \(42\cdot3=126\).
Missing: \(146-126=20\). Each cart adds \(4-3=1\).

steps.stem: A test has 25 questions, and Dana answers all of them. A correct answer gives 4 points, and a wrong answer takes away 1 point. Dana scores 70 points. How many of her answers are correct?
explanation: Assume all 25 are correct: \(25\cdot4=100\) points.
Each wrong answer changes \(+4\) into \(-1\): it costs 5 points. Lost: \(100-70=30\), therefore \(\frac{30}{5}=6\) wrong answers.

steps.stem: A train ticket costs 7 credits more than a bus ticket. Three train tickets and two bus tickets cost 81 credits altogether. What does a bus ticket cost?
explanation: Bus ticket \(=b\), train ticket \(=b+7\).
Assume all five tickets cost \(b\): the bill is \(3\cdot7=21\) lower, \(81-21=60\).

steps.stem: A club has \(m\) members. Each member pays 20 credits. The club uses this money to pay a hall fee of 150 credits. How much money is left per member?
explanation: Choose a number: \(m=10\). The club collects \(10\cdot20=200\) and pays 150. Left: 50, that is 5 per member.
Built directly: \(\frac{20m-150}{m}=20-\frac{150}{m}\).

steps.stem: At the end of each of 3 months, a reserve gives away \(\frac14\) of its remaining supplies. What fraction of the starting supplies remains after the third giveaway?
explanation: Each month \(\frac34\) of what is there stays.
After three months: \(\frac34\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac34=\frac{27}{64}\).
Not \(1-3\cdot\frac14=\frac14\): each quarter is taken from a smaller supply.

steps.stem: A potter sells \(\frac25\) of a batch, then \(\frac13\) of the pots left. Every pot has the same price. These sales bring in 360 credits. What would selling the entire batch bring in?
explanation: After the first sale, \(1-\frac25=\frac35\) of the batch is left. One third of it: \(\frac13\cdot\frac35=\frac15\).
Sold: \(\frac25+\frac15=\frac35\) of the batch, for 360 credits.
Whole batch: \(360\cdot\frac53=600\) credits.

steps.stem: A blend uses 3 parts juice and 5 parts water. How many liters of water must be added to 24 liters of the blend to make the ratio of juice to water \(1:3\)?
explanation: Juice: \(\frac38\cdot24=9\) liters. Water: \(24-9=15\) liters.
For the ratio \(1:3\), the water must be \(3\cdot9=27\) liters.
Add \(27-15=12\) liters of water.

steps.stem: 4 notebooks and 6 pens cost 50 credits together. All notebooks cost the same, and all pens cost the same. How much do 6 notebooks and 9 pens cost?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: One equation: \(4n+6p=50\). Divide by 2: \(2n+3p=25\).
We cannot find \(n\) or \(p\) alone, but this combination is a multiple of the equation.

steps.stem: A small storage box costs \(x\) credits. A large box costs \(\frac{x^2+32}{x}\) credits. The large box costs 3 times as much as the small one. How much does the small box cost?
explanation: Three times the small price is \(3x\): \(\frac{x^2+32}{x}=3x\).
A price is positive. Multiply both sides by \(x\): \(x^2+32=3x^2\).
Therefore \(2x^2=32\), \(x^2=16\) and \(x=4\) (a price cannot be \(-4\)).

steps.stem: Mira has \(n\) whole plums. She eats 4, gives half of the remaining plums to a neighbor, and uses 3 whole plums for a dessert. Which of the following could be the value of \(n\)?
explanation: After eating 4, she has \(n-4\) plums. Half of them must be a whole number. Therefore \(n-4\) is even, and \(n\) is even.
Only 12 is even. Check: \(12-4=8\). She gives away 4, keeps 4 and uses 3 ✓.

steps.stem: One large battery stores \(\frac54\) as much energy as one small battery. Which pack stores the most energy?
explanation: Plug in: a small battery stores 4 units, a large battery stores 5 units (\(\frac54\) of 4).
Choice (2), 6 large and 2 small, stores the most: 38 units.

steps.stem: Noah chooses a real number \(x\), divides it by 8, subtracts 3, multiplies by 6, and adds 18. The result is \(x\) again. What is \(x\)?
explanation: \(\frac34x=x\), therefore \(\frac14x=0\) and \(x=0\).

steps.stem: Ada starts work at 9 a.m. on each of five days. On three of those days she takes an unpaid one-hour break. She finishes at the same time every day and works 32 paid hours in total. When does she finish?
explanation: Time at work: \(32+3=35\) hours (32 paid hours and three unpaid breaks).
Each day: \(\frac{35}{5}=7\) hours.
Seven hours after 9 a.m. is 4 p.m.

steps.stem: Four years ago, a tree was 3 times as old as a shrub. Today the tree is twice as old as the shrub. How old is the shrub today?
explanation: Shrub now \(=s\), tree now \(=2s\). Four years ago: \(s-4\) and \(2s-4\).
The tree was 3 times as old. The \(\times3\) goes on the smaller side: \(2s-4=3(s-4)\).
\(2s-4=3s-12\), therefore \(s=8\). Check: four years ago 4 and 12 ✓.

steps.stem: One meter of silk costs \(x\) credits, and one meter of cotton costs \(y\) credits. The two prices add up to 17 credits, and silk costs 5 credits more than cotton. A shop sells \(x\) meters of silk (as many meters as the price of one meter) and buys \(y\) meters of cotton. What is the difference between the money received and the money spent?
explanation:
Write the two conditions:
\(\begin{cases} x+y=17 \\ x-y=5 \end{cases}\)
Add them: \(2x=22\), therefore \(x=11\) and \(y=6\).
Received: \(11\cdot11=121\). Spent: \(6\cdot6=36\).
Difference: \(121-36=85\) credits.

steps.stem: 3 notebooks and 2 pens cost 17 credits together. All notebooks cost the same, and all pens cost the same. How much do 2 notebooks and 3 pens cost?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: One equation, two unknowns: \(3n+2p=17\).
\(n=3\), \(p=4\) fits, and then \(2n+3p=18\). \(n=5\), \(p=1\) also fits, and then \(2n+3p=13\).
\(2n+3p\) is not a multiple of \(3n+2p\). It cannot be determined.

steps.stem: Two studios own the same number of brushes. One shares its brushes equally among 8 artists, and the other among 24 artists. Each artist in the first studio receives 3 times as many brushes as each artist in the second. How many brushes does each studio own?
choices: It cannot be determined from the information given.
explanation: Call the number of brushes \(B\). First studio: \(\frac{B}{8}\) each. Second studio: \(\frac{B}{24}\) each.
\(\frac{B}{8}=3\cdot\frac{B}{24}\) is true for every \(B\). The last sentence gives no new information.
Nothing fixes \(B\). It cannot be determined.

steps.stem: Three partners share a profit of 5,500 credits in the ratio of their investments. A invested twice as much as B, and B invested 1.5 times as much as C. How much does C get?
explanation: Give the plain unit to the smallest: C \(=2\) units, B \(=1.5\cdot2=3\) units, A \(=2\cdot3=6\) units.
The ratio of A to B to C is \(6:3:2\), in all 11 units. One unit: \(\frac{5{,}500}{11}=500\).
C gets \(2\cdot500=1{,}000\) credits.

steps.stem: A bag has red, green and blue marbles. The ratio of red to green marbles is \(5:2\). There are 1.5 times as many blue marbles as green marbles, and 12 more red marbles than blue marbles. How many marbles are in the bag?
explanation: Blue is 1.5 times green: the ratio of green to blue is \(2:3\).
Green is 2 in both ratios. The ratio of red to green to blue is \(5:2:3\).
Red minus blue: \(5x-3x=2x=12\), therefore \(x=6\).

steps.stem: Eight identical machines can finish a job in 15 hours. All eight start together. After 3 hours, 2 of the machines break down, and the others finish the job. How many hours does the whole job take?
explanation: The job: \(8\cdot15=120\) machine-hours.
First 3 hours: \(8\cdot3=24\) machine-hours are done. Left: \(120-24=96\).
Six machines: \(\frac{96}{6}=16\) more hours. Whole job: \(3+16=19\) hours.
The trap 20: \(\frac{120}{6}\) forgets that all eight machines worked for the first 3 hours.

steps.stem: A shop has \(n\) boxes with \(k\) pencils in each box. It sells 3 full boxes and 5 single pencils from another box. How many pencils are left in the shop?
explanation: Choose numbers: \(n=5\), \(k=10\). The shop has 50 pencils and sells \(3\cdot10+5=35\). Left: 15.
Built directly: \(nk-3k-5=k(n-3)-5\).

steps.stem: A parking garage charges 12 credits for the first hour or part of it, and 8 credits for every additional half-hour or part of it. How much does it cost to park for 2 hours and 50 minutes?
explanation: First hour: 12 credits.
Time left: 1 hour 50 minutes \(=110\) minutes. \(\frac{110}{30}=3\frac23\), and part of a half-hour is paid in full: 4 half-hours.
Total: \(12+4\cdot8=12+32=44\) credits.

steps.stem: In a box, the ratio of red balls to blue balls is \(5:6\). Then 4 red balls are taken out and 4 blue balls are put in. Now the ratio of red balls to blue balls is \(1:2\). How many red balls were in the box at first?
explanation: Red \(=5x\), blue \(=6x\). After the change: red \(5x-4\), blue \(6x+4\).
Blue is twice red: \(2(5x-4)=6x+4\), therefore \(10x-8=6x+4\) and \(x=3\).

steps.stem: Ben borrows some money and spends \(\frac25\) of it on rice. He repays his lender with \(\frac34\) of that rice at its purchase value. He still owes 8.40 credits. How much did he borrow?
explanation: Repaid with rice: \(\frac34\cdot\frac25=\frac3{10}\) of the loan.
Still owed: \(\frac7{10}\) of the loan \(=8.40\).
\(\frac1{10}\) of the loan \(=\frac{8.40}{7}=1.20\). The loan: \(10\cdot1.20=12\) credits.

steps.stem: A box of beads is split into two piles. One quarter of the first pile is used, and one sixth of the second pile is used. The two remaining piles contain 18 and 25 beads, in an unknown order. How many beads were in the box?
explanation: What is left of the first pile is \(\frac34\) of it, therefore it must be divisible by 3. 18 is divisible by 3, 25 does not.
First pile: \(\frac34F=18\), therefore \(F=18\cdot\frac43=24\).
Second pile: \(\frac56G=25\), therefore \(G=25\cdot\frac65=30\).
In the box: \(24+30=54\) beads.

steps.stem: A large kite’s tail is \(\frac38\) of its total length. A small kite’s tail is \(\frac14\) of its total length. The large tail is 9 times as long as the small tail. What is the ratio of the kites’ total lengths?
explanation: The large kite is \(L\) long and the small one \(S\): \(\frac38L=9\cdot\frac14S\).
Multiply by 8: \(3L=18S\), therefore \(L=6S\).
The ratio of the total lengths is \(L:S=6:1\).

steps.stem: A tutor changes every score by multiplying it by \(\frac35\) and then adding 24. June’s score goes down. Which of the following is necessarily true of her original score?
explanation: Unchanged score: \(\frac35x+24=x\), therefore \(\frac25x=24\) and \(x=60\).
Score goes down: \(\frac35x+24<x\), therefore \(24<\frac25x\) and \(x>60\).

steps.stem: Four positive numbers are arranged in two rows: a, b above c, d. The row totals are equal, and the column totals are equal. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
explanation:
Rows equal and columns equal:
\(\begin{cases} a+b=c+d \\ a+c=b+d \end{cases}\)
Subtract the second equation from the first: \(b-c=c-b\), therefore \(2b=2c\) and \(b=c\).
Put \(b=c\) into \(a+b=c+d\): \(a=d\).

steps.stem: There are \(n\) players in a room, where \(n\ge5\). Each player starts with \(2n\) tokens. The players leave the room one at a time. Just before leaving, a player gives 2 tokens to every other player still in the room. How many tokens does the fifth player to leave have left after giving out his tokens, as he leaves?
explanation: The first four players each give the fifth player 2 tokens: \(+8\). Before he gives, he has \(2n+8\).
When he leaves, \(n-5\) other players are still in the room. He gives each of them 2 tokens: \(-2(n-5)\).
Check with \(n=5\): he starts with 10, gets 8, and gives nothing (nobody is left): 18 ✓.
